description:
An implementation's amount that is a rounded printing of a number its own source states more precisely, and the precise value this list publishes instead. Read by `brightway_flows.lcia.precision`, applied to the consensus implementation only, and keyed on (category slug, substance) the way a ruling is -- the claim is about a substance in every compartment it is published in.

Both rows here are AR6 printing one assessment twice. Table 7.15, in the body of Chapter 7, states CFC-11's hundred-year global warming potential as `6226 ±2297` and HFC-134a's as `1526 ±577`. Table 7.SM.7, in the supplementary material, prints 6230 and 1530 -- the same assessment at three significant figures. EF 3.1 as the JRC published it carries the supplement's numbers; ecoinvent's implementation of the same method carries the chapter's. Where both speak the merge already keeps the precise one and calls it `agreed`; where only the JRC has a flow -- aircraft cruise height and indoor air -- the rounded number went out unopposed, so this list published 6230 for CFC-11 at cruise height and 6226 for CFC-11 everywhere else. One substance, one category, two numbers, and nothing on the page to say they are the same number. See #342.

`prints` is matched exactly rather than approximately. A row is a claim about one printed number, and a tolerance here would rewrite factors the row was never written about: 97 (substance, category) groups on the 2026-08-25 build publish two values agreeing within 2%, and 93 of them are freshwater ecotoxicity, where the two values are two compartments' own numbers and both are computed and correct.

`stated_about` records what every implementation stated when the row was written, and a build that states something else sends the question back rather than obeying a decision taken about other numbers -- the same contract `lcia-factor-rulings.json` and `lcia-misattributed-factors.json` hold.

What is deliberately not here: sulfur hexafluoride. Its two numbers are not one number printed twice. AR6 assesses SF6 with a 3200-year atmospheric lifetime and prints 25200 in Table 7.SM.7; ecoinvent's 24300 is AR6's own radiative efficiency with a lifetime near 1000 years, which reproduces their GWP-20 (18200), GWP-100 (24300) and GWP-500 (29000) to three significant figures where AR6's lifetime reproduces none of them. That is a disagreement about the atmosphere rather than about a printing, and it was settled by a ruling in `lcia-factor-rulings.json`.

printings.primary_source: IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 7, Table 7.15 (`6226 ±2297`); the rounded printing is Table 7.SM.7 (`6230`)
printings.comment:
CFC-11 is the reference substance of the ozone-depletion indicator and an ordinary greenhouse gas in this one; the number at issue is its GWP100. AR6 states it in two places. Chapter 7's Table 7.15, `Emission metrics for selected species`, prints `6226 ±2297` with the uncertainty the assessment carries. The supplementary Table 7.SM.7 prints `6230`, three significant figures of the same value, and the two captions say as much: 7.15's points at the supplement for the full table, and 7.SM.7 is that table.

The JRC's EF 3.1 states 6230 in all six air compartments; ecoinvent's implementation states 6226 in the four its own flow list has. In those four the merge already publishes 6226 as `agreed` -- 0.06% apart is inside `FACTOR_TOLERANCE`, and `agreed` keeps the more precise number. In the two ecoinvent has no flow for, aircraft cruise height and indoor air, the JRC is alone and 6230 went out as `sole`. This row publishes 6226 there too, so the substance carries one number.

What this does not claim is that the JRC transcribed anything wrongly: 6230 is exactly what Table 7.SM.7 prints, and their implementation goes on saying so under their own name. Nor is it a rule about numbers that are close. It is two documents, cited above, saying one thing at two precisions.

One caution for a reader checking the arithmetic against the supplement: 7.SM.7's CFC-11 row reads `5560`, not `6230`, because that row uses the unadjusted radiative efficiency of 0.259 W m-2 ppb-1. The 12% difference is the tropospheric adjustment, which Chapter 7 §7.3.2 assesses as non-zero for CFC-11 and which Table 7.15 includes -- 6226/5560 is 1.12. Both implementations use the adjusted value, so this row is about the rounding and not about that.

Another printing is not another row. If AR7 restates the substance, `stated_about` ends this claim rather than carrying it forward. (#342)

printings.primary_source: IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 7, Table 7.15 (`1526 ±577`); the rounded printing is Table 7.SM.7 (`1530`)
printings.comment:
HFC-134a is the refrigerant, and the case is CFC-11's exactly. AR6's Table 7.15 states its GWP100 as `1526 ±577`; Table 7.SM.7 prints `1530`, and the whole 7.SM.7 row -- lifetime 14 years, radiative efficiency 0.167, GWP20 4140 against the chapter's 4144 -- is the chapter's row at three significant figures.

The JRC states 1530 in six air compartments, ecoinvent 1526 in four, the merge publishes 1526 in those four as `agreed`, and this row publishes 1526 in the remaining two rather than leaving the substance with two numbers 0.26% apart.

Unlike CFC-11 there is no tropospheric-adjustment subtlety here: 7.SM.7's radiative efficiency and the chapter's are the same, and 1530 is 1526 rounded and nothing else. (#342)

printings.primary_source: IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 7, Table 7.15 (`6226 ±2297`); the rounded printing is Table 7.SM.7 (`6230`)
printings.comment: The fossil sub-category, which both implementations fill with the same number they state for the aggregate -- a synthetic halocarbon of industrial origin belongs in it, and neither publisher differentiates the two. Written as its own row rather than inferred from the aggregate's, because a category slug is what this file is keyed on and a substance that stopped being filed under `Climate change-Fossil` should stop being refined there rather than silently keep a rewrite. The reasoning is the row above's. (#342)

printings.primary_source: IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 7, Table 7.15 (`1526 ±577`); the rounded printing is Table 7.SM.7 (`1530`)
printings.comment: The fossil sub-category for HFC-134a. Both implementations file the refrigerant here with the number they state for the aggregate, as they do for every synthetic halocarbon, and this row refines the same two compartments -- aircraft cruise height and indoor air -- for the same reason: 1530 is Table 7.SM.7's three significant figures of the `1526 ±577` Table 7.15 assesses. Written out rather than deferred to the aggregate's row because this file is keyed on the category slug, and a substance that stopped being filed under `Climate change-Fossil` should stop being refined there rather than silently keep a rewrite nobody re-checked. (#342)
